verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ according to the commandment of God our Savior and the Lord Jesus Christ  our hope;
to Timothy, my true child in faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
As I urged you when I was going into Macedonia, stay at Ephesus that you might command certain men not to teach a different doctrine,
and not to pay attention to myths and endless genealogies, which cause disputes, rather than God’s stewardship, which is in faith —
but the goal of this command is love, out of a pure heart and a good conscience and sincere faith;
from which things some, having missed the mark, have turned aside to vain talking;
desiring to be teachers of the law, though they understand neither what they say, nor about what they strongly affirm.
But we know that the law is good, if a person uses it lawfully,

as knowing this, that law is not made for a righteous person, but for the lawless and insubordinate, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,
for the sexually immoral, for homosexuals, for slave-traders, for liars, for perjurers, and for any other thing contrary to the sound doctrine;
according to the Good News of the glory of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.
And I thank him who enabled me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he counted me faithful, appointing me to service;
although I was before a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent. However, I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
The grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.
However, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first, Jesus Christ might display all his patience, for an example of those who were going to believe in him for eternal life.
Now to the King eternal, immortal, invisible, to God who alone is wise, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
This instruction I commit to you, my child Timothy, according to the prophecies which led the way to you, that by them you may wage the good warfare;
holding faith and a good conscience; which some having thrust away made a shipwreck concerning the faith;
of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I delivered to Satan, that they might be taught not to blaspheme.

footnotes.content: Paul opens by calling Jesus 'our hope' — and this is the same Paul who once held the coats while Stephen was stoned. If God can rewrite a man like that into an apostle, nobody reading this in a low season is beyond rewriting. Hope wasn't Paul's personality. It was his assignment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul calls Timothy his 'true child in faith' — not by blood, but by grace. There's a tenderness here that only comes from walking together through hard things. We all need someone to call us that kind of family in the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul urges Timothy to stay put and guard the teaching at Ephesus. Sometimes faithfulness isn't going somewhere new, it's staying when it's easier to leave. Obedience can look like keeping watch.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Endless speculation pulls us away from God's work, which is built by faith. We can spend all our energy chasing questions that don't produce trust. The Lord's plan grows quietly where faith is simple.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'The goal of this command is love — from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith.' In an age when anyone can teach anything to everyone, Paul’s Ephesus warning travels well. This verse is the measuring stick for every voice — including these margin notes: does it produce love, or just noise?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It's easy to miss the mark by good intentions gone astray. We don't drift into love; we drift away from it when our hearts get tangled in talk. Grace calls us back to the simple goal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wanting to be a teacher is not wrong, but wanting to be a teacher before being a learner is dangerous. We do well to listen long before we speak. Humility keeps our footing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The law is good when used as it was meant to be used — not as a ladder to climb, but as a mirror to see our need. That need is exactly why grace matters so much.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul lists sins not to shame the broken, but to show what grace has rescued us from. We read this list and remember: if God forgave us, we have no right to look down on anyone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Any sin that crushes image-bearers stands against the God who made them. Yet the same God who calls it wrong also calls sinners to be made new. That tension is the heart of the gospel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The gospel isn't a self-help plan — it's the Good News of the glory of the blessed God. When we see his glory, our striving quiets. When we trust him, our hope holds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul thanks Jesus for counting him faithful and appointing him to serve. Notice: the faithfulness comes from being counted faithful by grace, not from earning it. That’s still how it works for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul doesn't downplay his past — he calls himself what he was. But mercy met him there. If mercy met Paul, it can meet us in the parts of our story we’d rather hide.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Grace didn't just cover Paul — it abounded. Faith and love came with it, gifts from Jesus himself. We don't muster them; we receive them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This is a saying worth leaning our whole weight on: Jesus came to save sinners. Paul calls himself the chief — not for false humility, but to make room for the rest of us. There’s room for you too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's patience with Paul was on display for all who would follow. He is just as patient with us. Our hope rests not on our perfection, but on his longsuffering love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After talking about a sinful man saved by mercy, Paul bursts into worship. The King who saves is eternal, immortal, invisible, and wise. Our hope is anchored in One who never fades.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul commits this charge to Timothy like a treasured heirloom. God had spoken over him, and now he passes it on. Faithfulness often looks like holding what others once entrusted to us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Faith and a good conscience must stay together. When we push conscience aside, faith doesn't usually die in a day — it shipwrecks slowly. Keep both close to Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul's discipline here is severe, but its goal is restoration — 'that they might be taught not to blaspheme.' Love can be firm. The goal is always to bring sinners back to the One who saves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
